summary: Feed s140_double is degraded for NDR: 12.4% of frames truncated to ~256B and 8.7% of TCP packets show missing data (sequence gaps). Both point to packet broker slicing/trimming that strips payload the NDR needs for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is slicing/trimming with small snaplen (~256B) causing TCP sequence gaps. Sequence analysis by IP length shows 170 of 1959 TCP packets (8.7%) with missing bytes, well above 1% threshold. Detail explicitly notes 'the feed is sliced' - slicing discards payload bytes and can also cause buffer drops.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs_full_payload=true and needs_both_directions=true; missing TCP bytes breaks stream reassembly, file extraction, and signature matching, causing missed detections and noisy retransmission handling.

recommended_fix.why: NDR supports up to 9216B and requires full payload. Disabling slicing restores complete TCP segments and eliminates the 8.7% sequence gaps.

findings.root_cause: Broker egress to NDR is configured to slice/trim packets to 256 bytes snaplen. 261 of 2105 frames (12.4%) are cut short, exceeding 5% threshold, most to exactly 256 bytes.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for deep packet inspection. Truncated frames hide L7 headers, URIs, certificates and malware payloads, blinding detection and forensics.

recommended_fix.why: Disable packet slicing/trimming on the broker port feeding this NDR and forward full frames (up to 9216B) to restore payload visibility.
